# Cortex XCOR Documentation

> Documentation for Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR and Palo Alto Networks Telemetry Pipeline: ingesting metrics, logs, traces, and change events; building dashboards and notebooks; alerting, SLOs, and incident response; controlling data volume and cost; and administering accounts, tools, and the Config, Data, and State APIs.

## Docs
- [Cortex XCOR documentation](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/index.md): Learn about the aspects of the Cortex XCOR documentation.

## Cortex XCOR

### Overview
- [Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/overview.md): Learn about Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR and its capabilities.
- [Get started with Cortex XCOR](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/overview/get-started.md): Learn about several of the common paths to complete tasks in Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR.

### Operator

### Navigate
- [Search for resources in Cortex XCOR](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/search.md): Use global search to find dashboards, monitors, services, SLOs, teams, and collections by name, and open Operator when you want to describe what you're looking for.
- [Use notebooks to gather related information](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/notebooks.md): Use notebooks to gather graphs, charts, and other resources from multiple pages into one place while troubleshooting a problem.
- [Filter across pages using pinned scopes](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/pinned-scopes.md): Learn about Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR cross-page filtering.
- [Reuse label selections with Quick filters](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/quick-filters.md)
- [Select time ranges](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/time-ranges.md): Use the time range selector to scope queries, charts, tables, and graphs across monitors, dashboards, service pages, and explorers.
- [Use comments to provide context](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/comments.md): Learn about how to use comments in Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR to identify important data.
- [Create favorites to find resources quickly](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/navigate/favorites.md): Mark dashboards and monitors as favorites to reach them faster from your personal home page, filtered resource lists, and search results.

### Identify trends

### Analyze data
- [Analyze live traffic metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/investigate/analyze/telemetry-analyzer.md): Use Live Telemetry Analyzer to view incoming metrics, troubleshoot ingest spikes, and identify metrics to reduce.

- [Analyze logs usage](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/investigate/analyze/logs-usage.md): Learn about utility scores and analyzing volume for log data in Cortex XCOR.
- [Analyze query load](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/investigate/analyze/query-analyzer.md): Use Query Analyzer to rank monitor and recording rule queries by relative load and assess which to modify.

- [Recording rules](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/control/shaping/shape-metrics/rules/recording.md): Learn about recording rules and when to use them, along with their limitations.
- [Mapping rules](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/control/shaping/shape-metrics/rules/mapping.md): Learn about how and when to use mapping rules before storing any results in the database.
- [Drop rules](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/control/shaping/shape-metrics/rules/drop-rules.md): Use drop rules to omit metrics you don't need and persist only the metrics that matter.

### Collector
- [CXDOT Collector integrations](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector.md): Use CXDOT Collector integrations to send telemetry data to Palo Alto Networks Cortex XCOR.
- [Apache](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/apache.md): Apache HTTP Server connection, request, traffic, and worker metrics.
- [cert-manager](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/cert_manager.md): Certificate lifecycle and expiry metrics from cert-manager, scraped from its controller's Prometheus endpoint.
- [ClickHouse](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/clickhouse.md): ClickHouse query, connection, merge, and replication metrics.
- [Consul](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/consul.md): Consul cluster and catalog health metrics from Consul agents.
- [Datadog](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/datadog.md): DogStatsD metrics, Datadog APM traces, and APM span metrics from apps instrumented with Datadog clients.
- [Docker](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/docker.md): Per-container CPU, memory, block I/O, network, process and uptime metrics from a Docker daemon, plus the daemon's own container and image counts.
- [Envoy](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/envoy.md): Envoy listener, cluster, and traffic metrics.
- [HAProxy](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/haproxy.md): HAProxy connection, request, and session metrics.
- [Host](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/host.md): Operating system metrics from the machine running the Collector, including CPU, memory, disk, file system, network, load, paging, process counts, and uptime.
- [HTTP Check](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/http_check.md): Availability, response time, and certificate expiry metrics for the HTTP endpoints your services depend on.
- [JMX](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/jmx.md): Runtime metrics from Java apps that expose Java Management Extensions.
- [Kubernetes](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/kubernetes.md): Kubernetes workload, node, cluster state, and control-plane metrics, and Kubernetes logs.
- [Memcached](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/memcached.md): Memcached cache, operation, and connection metrics.
- [MySQL](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/mysql.md): MySQL server performance and health metrics, including buffer pool, connections, commands, query throughput, and index usage.
- [NGINX](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/nginx.md): NGINX connection and request metrics scraped from the stub_status endpoint.
- [OpenMetrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/openmetrics.md): Metrics scraped from OpenMetrics and Prometheus endpoints.
- [OTLP](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/otlp.md): Logs, metrics, and traces ingested over the OpenTelemetry Protocol from instrumented apps.
- [PostgreSQL](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/postgres.md): PostgreSQL connection and workload metrics.
- [SNMP](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/snmp.md): Availability and performance metrics from SNMP network devices.
- [Apache Spark](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/spark.md): Apache Spark application metrics read from a driver's REST API, including executor memory and task throughput, garbage collection, shuffle volume, and persisted RDD storage.
- [TCP Check](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/tcp_check.md): Connectivity checks for TCP endpoints — whether a connection to each configured host and port can be established, how long the connect takes, and failed attempts by cause.
- [Temporal](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/temporal.md): Temporal request, workflow, task, and persistence metrics.
- [Apache Tomcat](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/tomcat.md): Apache Tomcat application and Java Virtual Machine runtime metrics collected over JMX.
- [Windows](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/xcor/integrations/collector/windows.md): Windows Event Log records, service-state metrics, and user-selected performance counters for Windows hosts, with per-channel, Service Control Manager, and per-counter-object target health.

### Chronosphere Collector

### Install
- [Install the Chronosphere Collector](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/metrics-traces/collector/install.md): Compare Chronosphere Collector installation methods for collecting metrics with Kubernetes or a standalone binary and for receiving traces.
- [Kubernetes Collector installation to retrieve metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/metrics-traces/collector/install/kubernetes.md): Install the Chronosphere Collector as a Kubernetes DaemonSet, Deployment, or sidecar to scrape Prometheus metrics from your cluster.
- [Kubernetes Collector installation to receive traces](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/metrics-traces/collector/install/tracing.md): Install the Chronosphere Collector as a Kubernetes Deployment to receive OpenTelemetry, Jaeger, or Zipkin trace data from your apps.
- [Standalone Collector installation to retrieve metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/metrics-traces/collector/install/standalone.md): Run the Chronosphere Collector as a standalone binary to gather metrics from services that Kubernetes doesn't manage.
- [Upgrade the Collector](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/ingest/metrics-traces/collector/install/upgrade.md): Upgrade the Chronosphere Collector to a new version.

## XCOR Academy
- [Academy](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy.md): Self-paced training on Chronosphere Observability Platform and Telemetry Pipeline, with links to related product documentation.

### Logs
- [Exploring Logs](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/exploring-logs.md): Est. ~20–40 minutes. Familiarize yourself with log querying and analysis tooling in the Observability Platform. Learn about log querying syntax, log visualizations for dashboards, and creating monitors to alert on log data.
- [Controlling Logs](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/controlling-logs.md): Est. ~20–40 minutes. Become versed in the Control Plane features of Logging in our Observability Platform. Explore concepts like partitions, control rules and budgets. Learn how to take advantage of Chronosphere's utilization analysis page to make decisions about your log data.
- [Exploring Logs 201](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/exploring-logs-201.md): Est. ~20–40 minutes. This 200-level course is a purely hands-on deep dive into writing advanced queries within the Chronosphere Observability Platform. Designed for users who already know their way around the Logs Explorer, this course focuses entirely on using query logic to troubleshoot issues and…

### Metrics
- [Introduction to PromQL](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/introduction-to-promql.md): Est. ~2 hours. Explore the foundations of the Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) and how you can use it to extract meaningful, actionable intelligence from your time series data. This is our 101 course, and it does not assume any prior knowledge of Prometheus.
- [Controlling Metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/controlling-metrics.md): Est. ~20–40 minutes. Dive into the fundamentals of controlling your metric data and cutting costs without compromising visibility. Learn how to use Chronosphere features to understand the utility of your data, apply shaping rules, and monitor usage and value over time.
- [Exploring Metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/exploring-metrics.md): Est. ~20–40 minutes. You're sending metric data to Chronosphere — now what?! This course goes over the basics of querying metrics, even if you haven't done any learning on PromQL. It also covers anomaly detection using Differential Diagnosis for Metrics.
- [PromQL 201](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/promql-201.md): Est. ~2 hours. Build on your PromQL fundamentals to make sense of complex queries, and craft your own. This course focuses on vector matching, logical operators, aggregations over time and a few other helpful functions.
- [Query Optimization for Metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/query-optimization-for-metrics.md): Est. ~2 hours. Dive into recording rules and derived telemetry to learn how they can help with query optimization. Learn how to identify the right optimization tool for your team's use case.
- [Working with Sparse Metrics](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/working-with-sparse-metrics.md): Est. ~15 minutes. This mini course explores the distinct challenges of working with metrics that don't report values at a regular interval. After exploring fundamental concepts about lookback windows and what it means to be sparse, learners will leave with several strategies in their toolbox for mit…

### Pipeline
- [Telemetry Pipeline](https://docs-xcor.paloaltonetworks.com/academy/courses/chronosphere-telemetry-pipeline.md): Est. ~2 hours. Learn the fundamentals of Telemetry Pipeline. You will build pipelines that collect telemetry data from a variety of sources, transforms it, and routes the data to various destinations.

Learn how to use Chronosphere features to understand the utility of your data, apply shaping rules, and monitor usage and value over time.
- [Controlling Traces](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~20–40 minutes. Explore more control features, this time for traces! You'll learn to create datasets and assign behaviors to those datasets to sample traces for datasets.
- [Creating & Tuning Monitors](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~20–40 minutes. Learn the ins and outs of alerting in Chronosphere, from templating notifications, to setting up monitor queries, to configuring signals, to iterating on conditions based on simulation and visualizations.
- [Creating & Tuning SLOs](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~20–40 minutes. How reliable is "reliable enough"? You will learn how to define specific target percentages that protect the user experience…

- [Exploring Metrics](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~20–40 minutes. You're sending metric data to Chronosphere — now what?! This course goes over the basics of querying metrics, even if you haven't done any learning on PromQL. It also covers anomaly detection using Differential Diagnosis for Metrics.

- [Introduction to Observability Platform](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~20–40 minutes. If you're onboarding onto our Observability Platform, this is a great place to start to learn how to navigate. Through a virtual lab, you'll take an interactive tour through a playground tenant that you'll revisit in future courses.
- [Introduction to PromQL](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~2 hours. Explore the foundations of the Prometheus Query Language (PromQL) and how you can use it to extract meaningful, actionable intelligence from your time series data. This is our 101 course, and it does not assume any prior knowledge of Prometheus.

- [PromQL 201](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~2 hours. Build on your PromQL fundamentals to make sense of complex queries, and craft your own. This course focuses on vector matching, logical operators, aggregations over time and a few other helpful functions.
- [Query Optimization for Metrics](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~2 hours. Dive into recording rules and derived telemetry to learn how they can help with query optimization. Learn how to identify the right optimization tool for your team's use case.

- [Telemetry Pipeline](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~2 hours. Learn the fundamentals of Telemetry Pipeline. You will build pipelines that collect telemetry data from a variety of sources, transforms it, and routes the data to various destinations.
- [Trusting Alerts: Troubleshooting Monitor Configuration](https://learn.chronosphere.io/): Est. ~15 minutes. The task of setting up monitors and tuning their thresholds is hardly trivial. This course focuses on strategies for tweaking our monitors so that we can ensure an alert triggers when a real problem exists.
